amundsen-gjoa-045.description: The Gjoa hard on a shoal with her sails set, captioned 'The "Gjoa" aground'. She struck a submerged reef north of Matty Island at six in the morning and lay on it through the day and night before a north gale flung her across it; the plate belongs to that passage through the shallow water east of King William Land. Amundsen gives no calendar date, but counting the mornings from his journal entry of 31 August 1903 puts the grounding on 2 September.
